rv.q: There's no doubting the talent and sincerity involved in Already Perfect, and Kreis himself brings a big voice to this small stage.
You'll rarely witness a better musical production at an intimate fringe venue, than this.

There is, understandably, a great deal of angst. And yet, if this all sounds like another earnest, existential gay-crisis musical, it really isn’t. One of the show’s great pleasures is its playful theatricality.
Already Perfect is hugely entertaining, with powerful songs that complement without swamping the action.
But in order to elevate Already Perfect above an extended therapy session, there needs to be more ambition pushing beyond the cliches.
Already Perfect feels like a monument to self-obsession as much as to survival, which makes it a little difficult to care…if it weren't for the songs.
Underlying the drama is a deep hankering for the bad old days when gay sex was taboo and when every fling was risky, rebellious and exhilarating.
The songs are what lifts Already Perfect.

cn.t: Critics praise Levi Kreis's semi-autobiographical musical for its personal storytelling and strong performances, though some question whether the intimate three-hander relies too heavily on its creator's central presence.
